title: La Bohème
synopsis: Set in 1830s Paris Latin Quarter, four young, impoverished bohemians—a poet, a painter, a musician, and a philosopher—navigate art, camaraderie, love, and tragedy in a freezing attic. When frail seamstress Mimì knocks on Rodolfo's door seeking a candle flame, an ardent passion blooms, set against Marcello and Musetta's stormy courtship and the bittersweet comedy of Bohemian camaraderie.

acts.title: Quadro Primo: In soffitta
acts.originalSetting: In soffitta. Ampia finestra dalla quale si scorge una distesa di tetti coperti di neve. A sinistra un camino. Una tavola, un letto, un armadietto, quattro sedie, un cavalletto da pittore con una tela sbozzata ed uno sgabello: libri sparsi, molti fasci di carte, due candelieri.
acts.setting: In the attic. A spacious window looks out upon an expanse of snow-covered rooftops of Paris. On the left a stove; a table, a bed, a cupboard, four chairs, a painter's easel with an unfinished canvas, and a stool. Books scattered about, bundles of manuscripts, two candlesticks.

cues.stageDirectionTranslation: on the landing, by the open door, holding high the candle

cues.speaker: Colline
cues.stageDirection: di fuori; Le voci di Marcello, Schaunard e Colline si fanno sempre più lontane
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: from outside; The voices of Marcello, Schaunard, and Colline grow ever more distant

cues.speaker: Schaunard
cues.stageDirection: Rumore d'uno che ruzzola .
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Sound of someone tumbling down.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: sull'uscio
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: at the door

cues.speaker: Colline
cues.stageDirection: lontano, dal basso della scala
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: distant, from the foot of the stairs

cues.speaker: Marcello
cues.stageDirection: più lontano; Rodolfo chiude l'uscio, depone il lume, sgombra un angolo del tavolo, vi colloca calamaio e carta, poi siede e si mette a scrivere dopo aver spento l'altro lume rimasto acceso: si interrompe, pensa, ritorna a scrivere, s'inquieta, distrugge lo scritto e getta via la penna.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: further away; Rodolfo closes the door, sets down the candle, clears a corner of the table, places inkwell and paper there, then sits down and begins to write after extinguishing the other candle: pauses, ponders, writes again, grows restless, destroys what he wrote and throws the pen away.

scenes.title: Non sono in vena / Chi è là?
scenes.titleTranslation: I am not in the mood / Who is there?
scenes.originalDescription: I compagni escono per festeggiare al caffè Momus. Rodolfo resta indietro per terminare un articolo. Bussano all'uscio: è Mimì con il lume spento.
scenes.description: The companions go out to celebrate at the Café Momus. Rodolfo stays behind to finish an article. A knock sounds at the door: it is Mimì with her candle blown out.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.literal: I am not in the mood.

cues.stageDirection: sfiduciato; Si bussa timidamente all'uscio.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: discouraged; A timid knock sounds at the door.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: di fuori
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: from outside

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: alzandosi
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: rising

lines.original: Di grazia, mi si è spento il lume.
lines.literal: Please, my candle has gone out.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: Corre ad aprire.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Hurries to open.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: sull'uscio, con un lume spento in mano ed una chiave
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: at the door, holding an extinguished candle and a key

lines.literal: Please come in for a moment.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: insistendo; Mimì, entra, ma subito è presa da soffocazione.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: insisting; Mimì enters, but is instantly seized with breathlessness.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: premuroso
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: solicitous

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: presa da tosse; Sviene, e Rodolfo è appena a tempo di sorreggerla ed adagiarla su di una sedia, mentre dalle mani di Mimì cadono candeliere e chiave.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: seized with coughing; She faints, and Rodolfo is just in time to support her and lay her on a chair, while candlestick and key fall from Mimì's hands.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.literal: And now what shall I do?...

cues.stageDirection: imbarazzato; Va a prendere dell'acqua e ne spruzza il viso di Mimì.; guardandola con grande interesse; Mimì rinviene.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: embarrassed; Goes to fetch some water and sprinkles it on Mimì's face; looking at her with deep interest; Mimì revives.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: con un filo di voce
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: in a faint voice

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.original: Qui c'è tanto freddo. Segga vicino al fuoco.
lines.literal: It is so cold here. Sit near the fire.

cues.stageDirection: Mimì fa cenno di no.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Mimì shakes her head no.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: Le dà il bicchiere e le versa da bere.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Hands her the glass and pours her a drink.

lines.literal: Just a little, just a little.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: Beve.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Drinks.

cues.speaker: Mimì

lines.original: che accenda il lume. È tutto passato.
lines.literal: to light my candle. It has all passed.

cues.stageDirection: Levandosi, cerca il suo candeliere.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Rising, she looks for her candlestick.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: Rodolfo scorge a terra il candeliere, lo raccoglie, accende e lo consegna a Mimì senza far parola.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Rodolfo notices the candlestick on the floor, picks it up, lights it, and hands it to Mimì without speaking a word.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: S'avvia per uscire.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Starts to leave.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: L'accompagna fino all'uscio.; Ritorna subito al lavoro.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Accompanies her to the door; Returns immediately to his work.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: Esce, poi riappare sull'uscio che rimane aperto.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Goes out, then reappears at the doorway which remains open.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.original: Non stia sull'uscio; il lume vacilla al vento.
lines.literal: Do not stand in the doorway; the flame flickers in the wind.

cues.stageDirection: Il lume di Mimì si spegne.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Mimì's candle goes out.

lines.literal: O God! Come light it again.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.original: Oh Dio!... Anche il mio s'è spento!
lines.literal: O God!... Mine has gone out too!

cues.stageDirection: Accorre colla sua candela per riaccendere quella di Mimì, ma avvicinandosi alla porta anche il suo lume si spegne e la camera rimane buia.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Hurries with his candle to relight Mimì's, but as he nears the door his candle also goes out and the room is plunged into darkness.

cues.speaker: Mimì

lines.literal: And where can the key be?...

cues.stageDirection: Avanzandosi a tentoni, incontra il tavolo e vi depone il suo candeliere.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Advancing gropingly, encounters the table and sets her candlestick upon it.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: Si trova presso la porta e la chiude.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Finds himself near the door and shuts it.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: Si volge dalla parte ove ode la voce di Mimì.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Turns toward the direction where he hears Mimì's voice.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: Ripete con grazia, avanzandosi ancora cautamente.; Cerca la chiave sul pavimento, strisciando i piedi.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Repeats with grace, still advancing cautiously; Searches for the key on the floor, dragging her feet.

lines.literal: What are you saying, not at all!

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: Urta nel tavolo, vi depone il suo candeliere e si mette a cercare la chiave brancicando le mani sul pavimento.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Bumps into the table, sets down his candlestick, and begins searching for the key, groping with his hands on the floor.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: Trova la chiave e lascia sfuggire una esclamazione, poi subito pentito mette la chiave in tasca.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Finds the key and lets slip an exclamation, then quickly repenting slips the key into his pocket.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: Cerca a tastoni.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Searches by touch.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: Finge di cercare, ma guidato dalla voce e dai passi di Mimì, tenta di avvicinarsi ad essa che, china a terra, cerca sempre tastoni: in questo momento Rodolfo si è avvicinato ed abbassandosi esso pure, la sua mano incontra quella di Mimì
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Pretends to search, but guided by Mimì's voice and footsteps, tries to draw near her as she, bent to the floor, keeps searching by touch: at this moment Rodolfo draws near and bending down himself, his hand touches Mimì's.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: sorpresa
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: surprised

scenes.title: Che gelida manina / O soave fanciulla
scenes.titleTranslation: What a frozen little hand / Oh lovely girl
scenes.originalDescription: Cercando al buio la chiave smarrita, le loro mani si toccano. Rodolfo racconta la sua vita da poeta e Mimì narra del suo lavoro di ricamatrice; sboccia un ardente amore che li unisce nell'andare insieme dagli amici.
scenes.description: Searching in the dark for the lost key, their hands touch. Rodolfo recounts his life as a poet and Mimì tells of her work as an embroiderer; an ardent love blossoms that unites them as they go together to join their friends.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.literal: Let me warm it for you.

lines.original: Cercar che giova? Al buio non si trova.
lines.literal: What is the use of searching? In the dark it cannot be found.

lines.original: Ma per fortuna è una notte di luna,
lines.literal: Yet luckily it is a moonlit night,

lines.original: e qui la luna l'abbiamo vicina.
lines.literal: and here we have the moon close beside us.
I will tell you in two words

lines.original: chi son, che faccio e come vivo. Vuole?
lines.literal: who I am, what I do, and how I live. May I?
Who am I? I am a poet.
What do I do? I write.
And how do I live? I live.
like a great lord I squander
and through castles in the air
two thieves steal all my jewels:
They entered just now with you,
Yet the theft does not grieve me,
for in their place has entered
it is your turn to speak. Who are you?

cues.stageDirection: tenendo la mano di Mimì, con voce piena di emozione!; Mimì tace: Rodolfo lascia la mano di Mimì, la quale indietreggiando trova una sedia sulla quale si lascia quasi cadere affranta dall'emozione.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: holding Mimì's hand, his voice full of emotion; Mimì is silent: Rodolfo releases her hand; stepping back she finds a chair and nearly collapses upon it, overwhelmed by emotion.

cues.speaker: Mimì

lines.original: ma il mio nome è Lucia.
è breve. A tela o a seta
lines.literal: is short. On cloth or silk
I embroider at home and abroad...
that speak of love, of springtime,

lines.original: quelle cose che han nome poesia...
lines.literal: those things that bear the name of poetry...

cues.stageDirection: È un po' titubante, poi si decide a parlare; sempre seduta.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: She hesitates a moment, then decides to speak; still seated.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: commosso
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: moved

lines.literal: the reason why I do not know.
I do not always go to mass,
yet I pray often to the Lord.
there in a little white room:

lines.original: guardo sui tetti e in cielo;
lines.literal: I look out over the roofs and into the sky;

lines.original: il primo bacio dell'aprile è mio!
lines.literal: the first kiss of April is mine!

lines.original: Germoglia in un vaso una rosa...
lines.literal: A rose buds in a vase...
Petal by petal I watch it!
is the perfume of a flower!

lines.original: Ma i fior ch'io faccio, ahimè! non hanno odore.
lines.literal: Yet the flowers that I make, alas! have no scent.

lines.original: Altro di me non le saprei narrare.
lines.literal: Other than this I could not tell you of myself.

lines.original: che la vien fuori d'ora a importunare.
lines.literal: who comes at an untimely hour to trouble you.

cues.speaker: Schaunard
cues.stageDirection: dal cortile
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: from the courtyard

cues.speaker: Marcello
cues.stageDirection: Alle grida degli amici, Rodolfo s'impazienta.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: At the shouts of his friends, Rodolfo grows impatient.

cues.speaker: Schaunard
cues.stageDirection: Sempre più impaziente, Rodolfo a tentoni si avvia alla finestra e l'apre spingendosi un poco fuori per rispondere agli amici che sono giù nel cortile: dalla finestra aperta entrano i raggi lunari, rischiarando così la camera.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Growing ever more impatient, Rodolfo gropes his way to the window, opening it and leaning out a little to reply to his friends below in the courtyard: moonlight pours through the open window, illuminating the room.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.original: Scrivo ancor tre righe a volo.
lines.literal: I am writing just three more lines in haste.

cues.stageDirection: alla finestra
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: at the window

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: avvicinandosi un poco alla finestra
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: approaching the window a little

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: a Mimì
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: to Mimì

lines.literal: You will get what is coming to you.

lines.original: Che te ne fai lì solo?
lines.literal: What are you doing there all alone?

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.original: Non sono solo. Siamo in due.
lines.literal: I am not alone. There are two of us.

lines.original: Andate da Momus, tenete il posto,
lines.literal: Go on to Momus, keep a table,

cues.stageDirection: Rimane alla finestra, onde assicurarsi che gli amici se ne vanno.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Remains at the window to make sure the friends depart.

cues.speaker: Tutti

lines.literal: quiet and discreet, let us be off.

cues.stageDirection: allontanandosi; Mimì si è avvicinata ancor più alla finestra per modo che i raggi lunari la illuminano: Rodolfo, volgendosi, scorge Mimì avvolta come da un nimbo di luce, e la contempla, quasi estatico.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: moving away; Mimì draws still nearer to the window so that the moonbeams shine full upon her: Rodolfo turns and beholds Mimì bathed as if in a halo of light, and contemplates her, almost ecstatic.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.original: O soave fanciulla, o dolce viso
lines.literal: Oh lovely girl, oh sweet face
bathed in the gentle glow of the lunar dawn,
in you I recognize the living

lines.original: il sogno ch'io vorrei sempre sognar!
lines.literal: dream that I would ever dream!

cues.stageDirection: cingendo con le braccia Mimì; La bacia.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: embracing Mimì in his arms; Kisses her.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: assai commossa; quasi abbandonandosi; svincolandosi
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: deeply moved; almost surrendering; disengaging herself

lines.literal: Your friends are waiting for you...

cues.speaker: Mimì

lines.literal: I should like to say... but I dare not...

cues.stageDirection: titubante
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: hesitant

cues.speaker: Mimì

lines.literal: What if I came with you?

cues.stageDirection: con graziosa furberia
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: with charming coquetry

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.literal: It would be so sweet to stay here.

cues.stageDirection: sorpreso; insinuante
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: surprised; insinuating

cues.speaker: Mimì

lines.literal: I shall be close beside you!...

cues.stageDirection: con grande abbandono
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: with great tenderness

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: maliziosa
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: mischievous

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.literal: Give me your arm, my little one.

cues.stageDirection: Aiuta amorosamente Mimì a mettersi lo scialle.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Lovingly helps Mimì put on her shawl.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: Dà il braccio a Rodolfo.; S'avviano sottobraccio alla porta d'uscita.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Takes Rodolfo's arm; Arm-in-arm they move toward the exit door.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: con abbandono
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: with devotion

acts.title: Quadro Secondo: Al Quartiere Latino
acts.originalSetting: Al Quartiere Latino. Una confluente di vie; all'incontro una piazza; botteghe, venditori di ogni genere; da un lato il caffè Momus. È la vigilia di Natale. Gran folla di popolo, borghesi, soldati, servette, ragazzi, studenti, sartine.
acts.setting: In the Latin Quarter on Christmas Eve. A bustling junction of streets forming a lively square flanked by shops and street vendors; on one side the Café Momus. A dense, festive crowd of citizens, soldiers, students, milliners, and children.

scenes.title: Aranci, datteri! Caldi i marroni!
scenes.originalDescription: La folla parigina anima la piazza tra le grida dei venditori ambulanti. Rodolfo compra per Mimì una cuffietta rosa; Colline compra una pipa e Schaunard un corno.
scenes.description: The Parisian crowd enlivens the square amid the cries of street vendors. Rodolfo buys a pink bonnet for Mimì; Colline buys a pipe and Schaunard a horn.

cues.speaker: Venditori
cues.stageDirection: sul limitare delle loro botteghe, altri aggirandosi tra la folla ed offrendo la propria merce
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: on the threshold of their shops, others moving through the crowd offering their wares

cues.speaker: Coro

lines.original: Quanta folla! Su, corriam! Che chiasso!
lines.literal: What a crowd! Come, let us run! What a racket!

lines.original: Stringiti a me. Date il passo.
lines.literal: Press close to me. Make way!

lines.original: Corri! Birra! Da ber! Un caffè!
lines.literal: Hurry! Beer! Something to drink! A coffee!

cues.stageDirection: studenti, sartine, borghesi e popolo; gridando e chiamando i Camerieri che vanno e vengono affaccendati
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: students, workgirls, citizens and common people; shouting and calling the waiters who bustle to and fro

cues.speaker: Coro

lines.literal: What a crowd, come, let us be off!

cues.stageDirection: allontanandosi
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: moving away

cues.speaker: Schaunard

lines.literal: This D is out of tune!
Pipe and horn, how much is it?

cues.stageDirection: dopo aver soffiato nel corno che ha contrattato a lungo con un venditore di ferravecchi; Paga .
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: after blowing into the horn which he bargained long for with a junk dealer; Pays.

cues.speaker: Colline

lines.original: ma è serio e a buon mercato...

cues.stageDirection: presso la rappezzatrice che gli ha cucito la falda di uno zimarrone; Paga, poi distribuisce con giusto equilibrio i libri dei quali è carico nelle molte tasche dello zimarrone .
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: at the mender's who has stitched the skirt of an old overcoat; Pays, then balances evenly the books he carries in the numerous pockets of the coat.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: A braccio con Mimì, attraversa la folla avviato al negozio della modista.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Arm in arm with Mimì, makes his way through the crowd toward the milliner's shop.

lines.literal: Shall we go for the bonnet?

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: Entrano in una Bottega di modista.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: They enter a milliner's shop.

cues.speaker: Marcello

lines.original: Io pur mi sento in vena di gridar:
lines.literal: I too feel in the mood to shout:

lines.original: Chi vuol, donnine allegre, un po' d'amor!
lines.literal: Who wants, merry maidens, a little love!

lines.original: Facciamo insieme a vendere e a comprar!
lines.literal: Let us buy and sell together!

cues.stageDirection: tutto solo in mezzo alla folla, con un involto sotto il braccio, occhieggiando le donnine che la folla gli getta quasi fra le braccia
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: all alone amidst the crowd, with a parcel under his arm, eyeing the girls whom the crowd almost pushes into his arms

cues.speaker: Venditori
cues.stageDirection: Entra un gruppo di venditrici.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: A group of female vendors enters.

cues.speaker: Marcello

lines.original: Io dò ad un soldo il vergine mio cuor!
lines.literal: For one penny I offer my virgin heart!

cues.stageDirection: La ragazza si allontana ridendo.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: The girl moves away laughing.

cues.speaker: Schaunard

lines.original: affretta la folla e si diletta

cues.stageDirection: Va a gironzolare avanti al caffè Momus aspettandovi gli amici: intanto armato della enorme pipa e del corno da caccia guarda curiosamente la folla.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Strolls in front of Café Momus waiting for his friends: meanwhile, armed with the enormous pipe and the hunting horn, looks curiously at the crowd.

cues.speaker: Colline
cues.stageDirection: se ne viene al ritrovo, agitando trionfalmente un vecchio libro.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: comes to the meeting place, triumphantly brandishing an old book.

cues.speaker: Marcello
cues.stageDirection: Arrivando al caffè Momus grida a Schaunard e Colline:
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Arriving at Café Momus, shouts to Schaunard and Colline:

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: uscendo dalla modista insieme a Mimì
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: emerging from the milliner's shop with Mimì

cues.speaker: Venditori
cues.stageDirection: alcuni
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: some

cues.speaker: Mimì

lines.original: Mi sta bene questa cuffietta rosa?
lines.literal: Does this pink bonnet suit me?

cues.stageDirection: accennando ad una cuffietta che porta graziosamente; Marcello, Schaunard e Colline cercano se vi fosse un tavolo libero fuori del caffè all'aria aperta, ma ve n'è uno solo ed è occupato da onesti borghesi. I tre amici li fulminano con occhiate sprezzanti, poi entrano nel caffè.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: pointing to a bonnet she wears charmingly; Marcello, Schaunard, and Colline look for a free table outside in the open air, but there is only one, occupied by respectable citizens. The three friends glare at them disdainfully, then enter the café.

cues.speaker: Ragazzi
cues.stageDirection: alcuni
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: some

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.original: Sei bruna e quel color ti dona.
lines.literal: You are a brunette and that color suits you well.

cues.stageDirection: a Mimì
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: to Mimì

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: ammirando la bacheca di una bottega
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: admiring a shop display window

cues.speaker: Rodolfo

lines.original: Ho uno zio milionario. Se fa senno il buon Dio,
lines.literal: I have a millionaire uncle. If the good Lord has sense,

lines.original: voglio comprarti un vezzo assai più bel!
lines.literal: I want to buy you a necklace far lovelier!

cues.stageDirection: Rodolfo e Mimì, in dolce colloquio, si avviano verso il fondo della scena e si perdono nella folla. Ad una bottega del fondo un venditore monta su di una seggiola, con grandi gesti offre in vendita delle maglierie, dei berretti da notte, ecc. Un gruppo di ragazzi accorre intorno alla bottega e scoppia in allegre risate.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Rodolfo and Mimì, in sweet conversation, move toward the back of the scene and lose themselves in the crowd. At a shop in the background a vendor climbs on a chair, with grand gestures offering knitwear, nightcaps, etc. A group of boys gathers around the shop and bursts into cheerful laughter.

cues.speaker: Ragazzi
cues.stageDirection: ridendo
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: laughing

cues.speaker: Studenti e Sartine
cues.stageDirection: accorrendo nel fondo presso i monelli ridendo
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: rushing into the background near the street urchins, laughing

cues.speaker: Borghesi

lines.literal: What a noise! What a crowd!
I am suffocating, let us go!
Let us go there to Momus!

cues.stageDirection: Entrano nel Caffè .
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Entering the café.

cues.speaker: Venditori
cues.stageDirection: Molta gente entra da ogni parte e si aggira per il piazzale, poi si raduna nel fondo. Colline, Schaunard e Marcello escono dal caffè portando fuori una tavola; li segue un cameriere colle seggiole; i borghesi al tavolo vicino, infastiditi dal baccano che fanno i tre amici, dopo un po' di tempo s'alzano e se ne vanno. S'avanzano di nuovo Rodolfo e Mimì, questa osserva un gruppo di studenti.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Many people enter from all sides and move around the square, then gather in the background. Colline, Schaunard, and Marcello come out of the café carrying a table; a waiter follows them with chairs; the citizens at the next table, annoyed by the noise of the three friends, after a while rise and leave. Rodolfo and Mimì advance again, the latter watching a group of students.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: con dolce rimprovero, a Mimì
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: with gentle reproach, to Mimì

lines.original: Odio il profano volgo al par d'Orazio.
lines.literal: I hate the profane rabble as Horace did.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: a Rodolfo
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: to Rodolfo

lines.original: All'uom felice sta il sospetto accanto.
lines.literal: Beside the happy man suspicion stands.

cues.speaker: Mimì
cues.stageDirection: a Rodolfo
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: to Rodolfo

cues.speaker: Marcello

Musetta, unable to walk having only one shoe on, is lifted onto the arms of Marcello and Colline, who break through the ranks of onlookers to follow the tattoo; the crowd, seeing Musetta carried triumphantly, takes occasion to give her clamorous ovations. Marcello and Colline with Musetta take their place at the tail of the tattoo, followed by Rodolfo and Mimì arm in arm, and Schaunard blowing his horn, then students and workgirls skipping merrily, then boys, citizens, and women falling into marching step. All this crowd moves away into the background following the military tattoo.

cues.stageDirection: Si avvicina a Mimì e le porge il manicotto.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Approaches Mimì and offers her the muff.

cues.speaker: Mimì

lines.original: Oh, come è bello e morbido! Non più
lines.literal: Oh, how beautiful and soft it is! No longer
shall my hands be pale and frozen. The warmth

cues.stageDirection: Aiutata da Musetta si rizza sul letto, e con gioia quasi infantile prende il manicotto.; a Rodolfo
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Helped by Musetta, sits up in bed, and with almost childlike joy takes the muff; to Rodolfo

cues.speaker: Musetta
cues.stageDirection: pronta
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: promptly

cues.speaker: Mimì

lines.literal: Thank you. But it must have cost dearly.
Are you weeping? I am well...
Here... my love... always with you!

lines.original: Le mani... al caldo... e... dormire.
lines.literal: My hands... warm... and... to sleep.

cues.stageDirection: Stende una mano a Rodolfo .; Rodolfo scoppia in pianto.; Mette le mani nel manicotto, si assopisce inclinando graziosamente la testa sul manicotto in atto di dormire.; Silenzio .
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Reaches out a hand to Rodolfo; Rodolfo bursts into tears; Puts her hands into the muff, dozes off gracefully inclining her head upon the muff as if asleep; Silence.

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: Rassicurato nel vedere che Mimì si è addormentata, cautamente si allontana da essa e fatto un cenno agli altri di non far rumore, si avvicina a Marcello.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Reassured seeing that Mimì has fallen asleep, cautiously moves away from her and gesturing to the others to make no noise, approaches Marcello.

cues.speaker: Musetta

lines.original: fate la grazia a questa poveretta
lines.literal: grant your grace to this poor girl
because the flame flickers in the draft.
And grant that she may recover.

cues.stageDirection: Fa scaldare la medicina portata da Marcello sul fornello a spirito, e quasi inconsciamente mormora una preghiera. Rodolfo, Marcello e Schaunard parlano assai sottovoce fra di loro; di tanto in tanto Rodolfo fa qualche passo verso il letto, sorvegliando Mimì, poi ritorna verso gli amici.; interrompendosi, a Marcello; Marcello si avvicina e mette un libro ritto sulla tavola formando paravento alla lampada.; Ripiglia la preghiera.; mentre Musetta prega, Rodolfo le si è avvicinato.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Heats the medicine brought by Marcello over the spirit stove, and almost unconsciously murmurs a prayer. Rodolfo, Marcello, and Schaunard speak in low whispers among themselves; from time to time Rodolfo takes a few steps toward the bed, watching Mimì, then returns to his friends; interrupting herself, to Marcello; Marcello approaches and stands a book upright on the table to shield the lamp; Resumes the prayer; while Musetta prays, Rodolfo approaches her.

lines.original: Io spero ancora. Vi pare che sia
lines.literal: I still have hope. Does it seem to you

cues.speaker: Schaunard
cues.stageDirection: Camminando sulla punta dei piedi va ad osservare Mimì, fa un gesto di dolore e ritorna presso Marcello. con voce strozzata; Intanto Rodolfo si è avveduto che il sole della finestra della soffitta sta per battere sul volto di Mimì e cerca intorno come porvi riparo; Musetta se ne avvede e gli indica la sua mantiglia, sale su di una sedia e studia il modo di distenderla sulla finestra. Marcello si avvicina a sua volta al letto e se ne scosta atterrito; intanto entra Colline che depone del danaro sulla tavola presso a Musetta.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Walking on tiptoe goes to observe Mimì, makes a gesture of grief and returns to Marcello; with choked voice; Meanwhile Rodolfo notices that the sunlight from the attic window is about to strike Mimì's face and looks around for a way to shade it; Musetta notices and points to her cloak, climbs onto a chair and studies how to drape it across the window. Marcello in turn approaches the bed and steps back terrified; meanwhile Colline enters and places money on the table near Musetta.

cues.speaker: Colline
cues.stageDirection: Poi visto Rodolfo che solo non riesce a collocare la mantiglia corre ad aiutarlo chiedendogli di Mimì
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Then seeing Rodolfo unable alone to fix the cloak runs to help him asking after Mimì

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: Si volge verso Mimì, in quel mentre Musetta gli fa cenno che la medicina è pronta, scende dalla scranna, ma nell'accorrere presso Musetta si accorge dello strano contegno di Marcello e Schaunard. con voce strozzata dallo sgomento
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Turns toward Mimì; at that moment Musetta signals to him that the medicine is ready, she steps down from the chair, but in hurrying toward Musetta he notices the strange demeanour of Marcello and Schaunard; with voice choked with terror

cues.speaker: Marcello
cues.stageDirection: Non regge più, corre a Rodolfo e abbracciandolo con voce angosciata grida:
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Unable to bear it any longer, rushes to Rodolfo and embracing him cries out in an anguished voice:

cues.speaker: Rodolfo
cues.stageDirection: Si precipita al letto di Mimi, la solleva e scotendola grida colla massima disperazione: piangendo; Si getta sul corpo esanime di Mimì Musetta, spaventata corre al letto, getta un grido angoscioso, buttandosi ginocchioni e piangente ai piedi di Mimì dalla parte opposta di Rodolfo. Schaunard si abbandona accasciato su di una sedia a sinistra della scena. Colline va ai piedi del letto, rimanendo atterrito per la rapidità della catastrofe. Marcello singhiozza, volgendo le spalle al proscenio.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Rushes to Mimì's bed, lifts her up and shaking her cries out in the deepest despair; weeping; Throws himself upon Mimì's lifeless body. Musetta, terrified, runs to the bed with an anguished cry, throwing herself on her knees weeping at Mimì's feet on the opposite side from Rodolfo. Schaunard sinks overwhelmed into a chair on the left of the stage. Colline stands at the foot of the bed, stunned by the swiftness of the catastrophe. Marcello sobs, turning his back to the footlights.
